With the AI assisted reverse engineering I was able to achieve such crazy reverse engineering succeses, in the last 6 months, which would take me years each on its own, if done by hands. Sometimes its a thin boundary between reverse engineering and software development. Sometimes you just decipher the proprietary save file format of the ugly paid app and then move into the clean software development phase of building your new, totally unique editor, to work with these files. (yes I made custom Photoshop too and its not the ArtCraft suite - I did it about a year before them, just for me). Reverse engineering and hacking into old softwares or devices has always been a hobby for me. I understand assembly, I understand hardware. But it was long and tedious process. With the cheap accesibility to smart LLM tools in these days, this hobby took dramatic turn for me. I do not miss manually analyzing the assembly instructions. But I love quickly getting the results. Yes my long experience helps me steer the agents the correct way. But that is also fun. And I am learning a ton of things along the way. I wish everyone would try to do some hacks of his own. For me the hobby is driven by curiosity. And LLMs didn't take that away. They gave me turbo boost to my wonderings and explorations. Let's free our minds!
